title: 8-bit Transformer Inference and Fine-tuning for Edge Accelerators
problem: Transformer models require significant computation and memory resources for inference and fine-tuning on edge accelerators. int8 quantization lacks precision and range for training, while prior FP8 approaches only quantize matrix multiplication inputs, leaving other operations at high precision.
motivation: Efficient inference and fine-tuning of transformers on resource-constrained edge accelerators is essential for deploying state-of-the-art NLP and vision models in edge environments.
method: Transformer models demand significant memory and computation, especially on small edge devices. This work compresses models using 8-bit floating-point (FP8) quantization—representing each number with just 8 bits instead of the standard 32 or 64 bits. Previous approaches only quantized matrix multiplication inputs while leaving other operations at full precision; this method quantizes all transformer operations. The result enables both inference and fine-tuning on edge accelerators while maintaining sufficient numerical precision for accuracy.
key_novelty: This work's single core idea is compressing all transformer operations into 8-bit floating-point for both inference and fine-tuning, whereas previous approaches only compressed matrix multiplication.
contributions: FP8 quantization scheme for transformer inference on edge accelerators
FP8 quantization methodology for transformer fine-tuning
Quantization of all transformer operations to maintain precision and range
